transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording available)
Attendees: Ethan Chen, Priya Rao, Marco Li — Vectora: Maya Patel, Jonas Reed, Lara Kim
Links referenced: pilot-pricing.xlsx, https://redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf, shared-traces.csv (customer link)

Summary:
Short postmortem follow-up after a 2/1 incident where a subset of requests experienced partial outputs / token alignment issues when we hit concurrent batching across quantized model variants. Today: walkthrough of repro status, short-term mitigations, and handoff of recovery playbook to Vectora ops + next steps for pilot.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and likely root cause (tokenization + batching boundary)
- KV cache / prefix-caching interactions on quantized runtime
- Temporary mitigations (per-route fallback to older model variant, burst cap config)
- Required customer traces and benchmarks for repro
- Security & compliance questions (data retention, audit logs)
- Pilot next steps and pricing

00:00 - Ethan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to make this a short ish call to hand over the recovery playbook and make sure the action items are clear.
00:16 - Maya Patel: Hi, thanks. we've been pretty nervous — some of our batch jobs started returning truncated responses and in prod that was... yeah not great.
00:32 - Priya Rao: quick primer, sorry, i'm priya, Solutions Eng on Redwood. We dug into the traces and there's a high signal that the issues happen when a request batch crosses a tokenization boundary and the quantized runtime emits token timing that the client misinterprets — so the client thought generation finished but actually there was a 0-token gap so streaming cut off.
00:50 - Jonas Reed: right, we saw that in partner logs — some of our workers timeout after 800ms and then drop the stream. on the customer side it looks like partial payloads. is that the kv cache?
01:05 - Priya Rao: Not just KV cache, jonas — it's an interaction: prefix caching plus continuous batching + quantization path created an edge where token offsets were misaligned. sometimes the KV cache would serve a prefix that assumed a different tokenization mapping for that quantized kernel. audio to text? no, bad analogy, sorry.
01:22 - Lara Kim: can you say that again, the "tokenization mapping" piece?
01:30 - Priya Rao: Yeah. some quantized kernels use an alternate token split at the byte level — in 8-bit paths we saw a different segmentation for a tiny subset of unicode sequences. when the runtime stitches KV cached prefix + live decode, the offsets didn't line up so the client observed an early EOS.
01:52 - Maya Patel: aha okay, that matches our samples. we have about 12 distinct cases in the traces where the response ends mid-sentence.
02:10 - Ethan Chen: quick note on severity and scope: only requests hitting the dedicated quantized pool under high concurrency, roughly 2% of traffic in the window. this is why your intermittent error rate spiked but most calls were fine.
02:28 - Jonas Reed: we have a question on rollback: you suggested fallbacks to older model variants in the incident. what's the impact on latency/cost?
02:37 - Priya Rao: fallback to the non-quantized variant adds about 40-60ms median latency in our tests and about 12-18% cost increase per-token in that path. but it avoids the token mapping edge. a temporary policy could be: detect batch-boundary risk and route those requests to non-quantized model.
03:00 - Lara Kim: would that be automatic in your platform or do we need to change client code?
03:08 - Priya Rao: Redwood routing can do it server-side via a per-route rule; no client code changes required. we can ship a canary that sets a request header and redirects based on sequence length distribution.
03:22 - Maya Patel: okay, what do you need from us to validate?
03:30 - Priya Rao: sample traces (anonymized) + a small replay harness. if you can share a 30 minute window of request/response pairs and the token offsets, SE can run a controlled repro.
03:45 - Jonas Reed: we can extract that, i'll scrub PII and send a filtered csv.
03:52 - Ethan Chen: noted — we'll include a template for the traces in the email.
04:05 - Marco Li: also, Marco from CS — quick ops question: do you want a hotfix that's a config change or we push a binary patch to runtime?
04:15 - Priya Rao: both possible. short term: a routing + model-variant fallback is config-only and can be applied in minutes. medium term: runtime patch to unify tokenization mapping in quantized kernels (requires code + perf validation). long term: add a per-request checksum on KV cache hits to validate mapping.
04:40 - Lara Kim: checksum on cache hits, is that heavy?
04:44 - Priya Rao: it's lightweight if we do a short token-prefix fingerprint; cost negligible compared to token generation. but it needs careful rollout.
05:00 - Maya Patel: what's the timeline for the medium term fix?
05:05 - Priya Rao: our engineering rough estimate is 3-4 sprints to implement and harden the quantized kernel mapping, then another sprint for regression. so 8-10 weeks, conservative.
05:22 - Jonas Reed: do you have a reproduction internally?
05:25 - Priya Rao: yes, lab repro for about 80% of cases using the sample inputs we saw. but we need your traces to hit the last 20% — edge unicode sequences.
05:42 - Ethan Chen: pedantic note: the issue only replicates under a specific batching pattern — if you throttle concurrency slightly it won't reproduce. so there's a mitigation of setting a temporary burst cap.
05:58 - Lara Kim: burst cap — what effect on throughput?
06:03 - Priya Rao: reducing the burst cap to 8 from 32 cut reproducer probability in our tests with minimal throughput impact for your load (it mildly increases p99 latency during spikes).
06:18 - Maya Patel: alright. security questions: our InfoSec wants to confirm audit logs and retention. is there a place where we can see the request-level audit for dedicated?
06:30 - Ethan Chen: yes, Dedicated and Private both expose audit logs; we'll include the SOC2/ISO packet and a doc on how long logs are retained and how to configure retention in VPC packages.
06:45 - Maya Patel: and for pilot pricing?
06:48 - Ethan Chen: i'll send the pilot pricing workbook after this call, also include a suggested sizing to avoid hitting the quantized pool hotspot.
07:02 - Jonas Reed: do you recommend sticking with Dedicated for now or go Private?
07:08 - Priya Rao: Dedicated gives us direct control over GPU pools and we can pin non-quantized variants; Private gives more network isolation but longer lead time. For immediate mitigation Dedicated + routing rules is fastest.
07:25 - Lara Kim: any compliance blockers with sending traces?
07:29 - Marco Li: we'll provide a template, we ask for hashed user ids and filtered payloads, that usually satisfies legal.
07:35 - Maya Patel: agreed we'll scrub.
07:40 - Ethan Chen: okay, moving to the playbook we prepared — i'm going to walk through high-level steps and who owns them.
07:48 - Ethan Chen: Step 1: Apply route-level fallback rule to non-quantized variant for requests > X tokens or known prefix patterns. Target: within 24 hours of approval.
08:02 - Priya Rao: Step 2: apply temporary burst cap on the dedicated pool to reduce cross-batch mixing. Target: within 4 hours.
08:12 - Priya Rao: Step 3: SE runs controlled repro using your traces and returns logs + flag hits. Target: 3 business days.
08:22 - Maya Patel: sounds good. Step 4?
08:25 - Priya Rao: Step 4: Roll runtime patch to align token mapping if repro confirmed. This is the 8-10 week path.
08:34 - Jonas Reed: and what about rollback if the patch creates regressions?
08:37 - Priya Rao: we keep pinned model variants and kernel selection per machine; rollback is an immediate routing change. you can pin all traffic to the stable (non-quant) variant while we iterate.
08:52 - Maya Patel: are there monitoring flags we should enable?
08:55 - Priya Rao: yes, enable the new 'prefix-mismatch' metric in the console and set alert on >0.5% mismatches per minute. we'll share a dashboard template.
09:10 - Ethan Chen: ok, i'm going to read the next steps and then we'll open for Qs.
09:16 - Ethan Chen: Next steps: 1) Priya to run repro and share logs by 2027-02-08; 2) Ethan to email pilot pricing + SOC2 docs by 2027-02-05; 3) Vectora to send traces by 2027-02-06.
09:30 - Maya Patel: agreed. any blockers for us to do the route rule?
09:34 - Priya Rao: none, we can apply it as a canary on a small subset of traffic and watch.
09:40 - Lara Kim: ok do that.
09:42 - Jonas Reed: quick note — are there any long tail concerns around language coverage? we saw most cases in emojis and CJK.
09:52 - Priya Rao: yes, edge unicode sequences like zero-width joiners and certain emoji clusters triggered the segmentation difference. we'll flag these in the repro.
10:06 - Ethan Chen: i'm going to pause the transcript here and summarize the remainder of the conversation which had deeper engineering detail and log walk-throughs.
10:12 - [10:12-40:00] Deep log walkthrough (SEs and Vectora SREs). Topics covered: specific request ids, sample token offsets, KV cache hit telemetry, per-kernel tokenization differences, and a short live demo of the repro harness. There was some cross-talk and a few mis-heard words recorded ("KV cash" appears twice in logs).
40:05 - Priya Rao: lab repro demonstrated 78% of cases; the 22% remain tied to combined edge unicode + specific batch windowing. we pushed a temporary canary routing and saw failures drop to ~0.2% in the canary group.
41:10 - Maya Patel: that's promising. what do you recommend for the pilot acceptance criteria?
41:18 - Ethan Chen: acceptance: error rate < 0.3% for 7 consecutive days on real traffic with canary routing, and no production regressions on latency beyond a defined SLA. we'll formalize this in the pilot doc.
41:35 - Lara Kim: also need confirmation that audit logs capture the changed routing for compliance audit.
41:42 - Marco Li: yes, routing changes are auditable and we can export the change history for your auditors.
42:00 - Jonas Reed: any competitors mentioned? Maya: we looked at CloudModelInc but their pricing and infra didn't fit our latency profile.
42:15 - Priya Rao: small aside — we ran a perf diff with NimbusAI on a subset; Nimbus did not show the quantization mismatch but has different throughput/cost tradeoffs.
42:30 - Ethan Chen: wrapping up — i'll send an email with the playbook, the pricing workbook, and the trace template. we'll schedule a tech deep dive next week if vectora wants to watch the repro run live.
42:44 - Maya Patel: yes let's schedule the tech deep dive, please include our SREs.
43:00 - Lara Kim: one more compliance Q: are there encryption options for logs in transit to your S3?
43:07 - Ethan Chen: yes TLS and we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments; we'll include the config doc.
43:18 - Jonas Reed: thanks, that's helpful.
43:22 - Ethan Chen: final recap of action items and owners... (see action items list sent in follow-up).
43:30 - Maya Patel: thanks team, appreciate the speedy response.
43:35 - Marco Li: We'll keep an eye on the canary and update you in slack.
43:40 - Priya Rao: quick note: we'll also propose a temporary dashboard and alert thresholds in the next 24 hours.
43:50 - Ethan Chen: Great, thanks everyone. End of call.

Notes after call (SE follow-up):
- SE confirmed lab repro artifacts attached to ticket ff-784321.
- Repro harness notes: uses the customer's token offsets and a small randomized batch window to surface mismatch.
- Temporary mitigations applied: canary route to non-quantized variant (reduced failures to 0.2%); burst cap set to 8 on dedicated pool for canary.
- Long-term plan: kernel alignment patch (8-10 weeks) + cache fingerprinting feature (TBD).

Attachments referenced in email follow-up: pilot-pricing.xlsx, redwood-security-pack.pdf, vectora-trace-template.csv
